newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks climb, construction, OTE shares jump.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks climb, construction, OTE shares jump.

text.p: Greek shares ended above 1,000 points for the second consecutive session on Thursday climbing 1.01 percent and market watchers expected the advance to continue as investors viewed equities as an investment opportunity.

"Greek and foreign investors view the Athens bourse as a good investment opportunity because it is a cheap market with a low price earnings ratio (P/E) and high dividend yields," said Aspis Securities chief analyst John Kanellopoulos.
He added that the overall market sentiment was positive, building on optimistic forecasts of diminishing inflation and cuts in interest rates.
The Athens general share index closed up 1.01 percent or 10.09 points at 1012.39 from Wednesday's 1002.30. It opened at 1001.75.
Shares of OTE and major construction companies like Aegek and Michaniki rose strongly.
"I believe the major reason behind OTE's rise was the news for high profits in 1997," another broker said.
He explained that the turn towards construction shares and away from banks was a typical market move.

"Usually, when a sector has performed quite well for some time, like banks, stocks become expensive and people divert to cheaper shares. This is what happened with shares of Aegek and Michaniki, which were undervalued," he added.
Thursday's turnover of 10.7 billion drachmas was quite satisfactory, market watchers said. Gainers led losers 113 to 94 with 27 issues unchanged on 234 traded.

Banks lost 0.89 percent, construction jumped 3.33 percent while small caps rose by 0.72 percent. Industrials closed 0.99 percent higher along with investment and leasing shares which closed up 0.05 and 0.14 percent.
